stories.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
stories.description: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
stories.acGateReason: Auto-elaborated from description (original verdict: insufficient). The acceptance criteria field is empty ('(none)') and the description provides only a vague user story with no testable specifics, making implementation direction ambiguous across three codelines.
verificationCriteria: When an editor saves a change to page content in the Contentstack CMS, the corresponding rendered page updates to show the new content without the tester reloading the browser or navigating away.

When an editor saves a change to page content in the Contentstack CMS, the previously displayed content is no longer shown on the page in place of the updated content (no stale or duplicated rendering of the old value).
When an editor saves a change to content used on a GO Transit page in the Contentstack CMS, the GO Transit page displays the updated content without a manual browser reload.
When an editor saves a change to content used on a UP Express page in the Contentstack CMS, the UP Express page displays the updated content without a manual browser reload.
When an editor saves a change to content used on an MX page in the Contentstack CMS, the MX page displays the updated content without a manual browser reload.
When no CMS content change has been saved, the rendered page continues to display its initial content unchanged and without errors, flicker, or repeated re-rendering.

When the application runs without live preview active (e.g. a normal visitor session outside the CMS editing environment), the page still renders its published content correctly and no errors or blank regions appear on the displayed page.

fixSiteAnalysis.reason: This is where the Contentstack content state is created and provided to the entire app. It currently uses useMemo to produce a static context value from defaultContent, which never updates when the Contentstack SDK fires live-preview callbacks. The live_preview config is already passed to contentstack.Stack() in src/services/contentstack.ts, but the app never registers the Stack.livePreview(onEntryChange) callback that the SDK provides to push updated entries — so the context value is frozen and editors never see changes without a full reload.
fixSiteAnalysis.fix: Replace the useMemo with useState initialized from defaultContent, and register Stack.livePreview with an onEntryChange callback that merges the updated entry into the content state (triggering a React re-render). Import Stack from 'services/contentstack'. The Contentstack SDK's livePreview method accepts an onEntryChange callback; when it fires, spread the incoming entry data into the existing content state. This is the minimal change: the Stack already has live_preview configured (CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN, CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_ENABLE, CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST env vars in src/services/contentstack.ts lines 24-26,63-67) — the provider just needs to subscribe to its update events.

specification.coordinatorNotes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no prior spec work (spec: null). It describes a complex multi-domain CMS live preview feature spanning GO, UP, and MX, requiring full elaboration (AC definition, story split proposals, technical depth) followed by hardening (testability criteria, security checks, edge cases). Both agents assigned in order: openspec first, then speckit reviews its output.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — live preview does not yet function end-to-end. The SDK config at src/services/contentstack.ts already declares live_preview fields but useContent.ts does not react to preview events. Attachment points are the Stack config and the useContent hook. Verification criteria derived entirely from description since ACs are empty.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all criteria were created from scratch based on the story title/description and openspec's notes about attachment points (Stack config at src/services/contentstack.ts, useContent hook). I could not review the actual file contents of src/services/contentstack.ts or useContent.ts, which may contain existing live_preview config fields and hook signatures that would refine these criteria further — for example, the exact query parameter names, token format, or event shape. Criteria cover: core real-time update behavior (AC-1), mode gating (AC-2, AC-3), atomicity (AC-4), connection failure (AC-5), malformed data (AC-6), content-type mismatch (AC-7), security/token validation (AC-8), accessibility — screen reader (AC-9) and visual (AC-10), nested/referenced content (AC-11), and route persistence (AC-12).

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents ran to completion but produced no persisted deliverables. OpenSpec was assigned to elaborate ACs and propose story splits for a complex multi-domain (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature, yet it returned acceptanceChanged: false and splitCount: 0 — only observational notes about attachment points (contentstack.ts config, useContent hook). Speckit then claimed to author 12 acceptance criteria (AC-1 through AC-12 covering real-time updates, mode gating, atomicity, failure handling, security, accessibility, nested content, route persistence) but also reports acceptanceChanged: false, and the acceptanceCriteria array remains empty []. This is contradictory: either the criteria were authored but not persisted (tooling failure), or Speckit only described them in prose without writing them. Either way, the structured output is missing. Additionally, no story splits were proposed despite the coordinator's own notes flagging this as a complex multi-domain feature that likely warrants decomposition. Speckit also admitted it could not access the actual source files (src/services/contentstack.ts, useContent.ts), meaning its criteria were derived from the story title and OpenSpec's notes rather than grounded in the codebase. Human review is required to: (1) determine why criteria weren't persisted, (2) validate the 12 proposed criteria against actual SDK config and hook signatures, (3) decide whether this story should be split by domain or concern.
